guard_patterns.handling: Require directly accessible official public source.
Preserve publication edition and reference period.
Keep activity, installations, energy and emissions distinct.
Keep modelled, estimated, reported and measured values distinct.
Preserve UK, GB, England, local-authority, installation, operator and parcel boundaries.
Retain provisional, correction and revision status.
Preserve kWh, GWh, tonnes, units, CO2e, thresholds and scheme scopes.
Retain coverage changes, exclusions, thresholds and suppression limits.
No parcel value without parcel identity, geometry, activity and compatible method binding.
Every package must pass deterministic structure and scope checks.

packages.title: Subnational electricity/gas administrative-meter scope QA
facts: DESNZ provides annual electricity and gas estimates below national level.
The latest reviewed summary covers 2024.
The estimates use industry administrative meter-point data.
The statistics are accredited official statistics.
Outputs include country, region and local-authority geographies.
Consumption is activity data, not direct GHG measurement.
Meter points do not by themselves identify cadastral geometry.
Domestic/non-domestic labels are statistical classifications.
Publication year and reference year must remain separate.
Parcel emissions require parcel-specific activity and attribution.

packages.title: Subnational gas domestic-threshold guard QA
facts: Gas meters below 73,200 kWh per year are classed domestic in this dataset.
Meters at or above 73,200 kWh are classed non-domestic.
The threshold is an industry classification convention.
Some small commercial properties can appear as domestic.
Threshold crossing can distort non-domestic meter-count trends.
Threshold crossing can distort non-domestic mean and median trends.
Total-consumption changes are less sensitive to this issue.
Domestic label does not prove residential parcel use.
Non-domestic label does not identify a business parcel.
Parcel classification must remain separate from meter classification.

packages.title: Subnational gas unique-site exclusion QA
facts: DESNZ receives data for high-consuming Unique or Non-Standard Sites.
These sites can have complex billing arrangements.
Unique-site consumption is excluded from the published subnational gas series.
The exclusion preserves time-series consistency.
Published local totals are therefore not exhaustive of all high-consuming sites.
Excluded sites must not be reconstructed from local averages.
Consistency and completeness are separate quality dimensions.
High-consuming exclusions can matter to industrial interpretation.
A local total is not exhaustive parcel coverage.
Parcel estimates must preserve this exclusion limitation.

packages.title: Subnational gas time-base/weather-correction QA
facts: The 2024 summary presents weather-corrected gas consumption.
Gas-year timing has changed historically.
From 2019 onward the gas year uses a mid-May to mid-May convention.
Gas reference periods are not identical to calendar years.
Weather correction affects trend interpretation.
Gas-year activity should not be merged blindly with calendar-year emissions.
Reference-period metadata is required for derived calculations.
Weather-corrected activity differs from raw billed consumption.
Time-base mismatch can create false trend signals.
Parcel calculations require compatible temporal alignment.

packages.title: Subnational electricity local-authority versus parcel QA
facts: DESNZ publishes electricity consumption at region and local-authority level.
The series includes domestic and non-domestic statistics.
The source uses electricity meter-point administrative data.
Local-authority outputs are aggregated geographic statistics.
An area value does not identify individual parcels.
Area mean consumption is not a parcel measurement.
Area totals should not be divided across parcels without a method.
Electricity consumption and electricity emissions are different quantities.
An emissions factor is a separate methodological input.
Parcel emissions remain unbound without parcel activity evidence.

packages.title: Subnational gas revision-notice QA
facts: DESNZ issued a gas-statistics revision notice in May 2026.
A December 2025 correction affected 2023 non-domestic gas for one North East area.
That correction concerns 2023 rather than 2024.
Revision history is part of source provenance.
Previously downloaded tables can become stale.
Year-specific corrections must not be generalized to other years.
Revised values supersede older values for corrected periods.
Version date must accompany downstream calculations.
A corrected area value is still not a parcel measurement.
QA must check revision status before historical reuse.

packages.title: ONS total energy-use residence-basis QA
facts: ONS released the current total-energy-use dataset on 5 June 2026.
The dataset covers 1990 to 2024.
It reports direct UK energy use from fossil and other sources.
Total energy includes nuclear, net imports, renewables, biofuels and waste.
Energy is reallocated by SIC 2007 industry sections.
The dataset belongs to UK Environmental Accounts.
Environmental-account energy is not a territorial parcel inventory.
Industry attribution follows statistical accounting concepts.
Energy use and GHG emissions are distinct measures.
Parcel inference needs separate geographic/activity binding.

packages.title: ONS industry/source/fuel dimensionality QA
facts: ONS publishes energy use by industry, source and fuel.
The current edition was released 5 June 2026.
The dataset covers roughly 130 SIC industry groups.
It distinguishes around 80 source categories.
It distinguishes around 20 fuel categories.
Sources include combustion, aircraft and road transport categories.
Fuels include categories such as peat and natural gas.
Dimensions must not be collapsed without documented aggregation.
A national industry-fuel cell is not a parcel observation.
Parcel emissions need compatible local activity evidence.

packages.title: ONS fossil-fuel table exclusion QA
facts: ONS publishes fossil-fuel energy use by fuel type and industry.
The current edition was released 5 June 2026.
It includes coal, natural gas, petrol, road diesel and aviation fuel categories.
The table excludes biofuels and waste.
This exclusion changes meaning relative to total-energy tables.
Fossil-fuel totals must not be described as all-energy totals.
Fuel definitions must be preserved downstream.
National fuel data do not identify parcel consumption.
Energy use is not direct emissions measurement.
Emissions conversion needs factors plus parcel activity provenance.

packages.title: ONS energy revisions/method-error guard QA
facts: ONS dataset pages provide previous editions.
Initial estimates can be revised as more data become available.
Statistics can also change when methods or systems change.
Planned revisions differ from corrections of genuine errors.
ONS explains genuine corrections when identified.
Dataset edition date is required provenance.
Old and current editions must not be silently mixed.
Method revisions can affect comparability.
Revision control does not create parcel evidence.
QA separates version validity from geographic attribution.

packages.title: Solar PV deployment capacity-versus-generation QA
facts: DESNZ solar PV statistics report monthly deployment.
The dataset is published by capacity and accreditation.
The reviewed dataset was updated 30 June 2026.
It is included in Energy Trends table ET 6.3 from June 2026.
The data are accredited official statistics.
Installed capacity is not electricity generation.
Accreditation status is not emissions measurement.
Deployment does not identify a parcel without location binding.
Installed PV does not prove displaced-grid emissions.
Parcel carbon needs generation, time-base and attribution evidence.

packages.title: Solar PV monthly-lag/accreditation QA
facts: The reviewed solar-PV data run through May 2026.
The series is monthly rather than real-time.
Publication therefore lags the latest deployment month.
Capacity and accreditation are distinct fields.
Accredited-installation count is not a generation meter reading.
Monthly deployment is not annual generation.
Publication date and data-through date must both be retained.
Future release announcements are not published observations.
Deployment is infrastructure/activity evidence, not parcel emissions.
Parcel use requires explicit installation-to-parcel binding.

packages.title: Heat-pump hydronic 45kW scope QA
facts: DESNZ heat-pump statistics monitor hydronic heat pumps up to 45 kW.
The collection includes air-source and ground-source heat pumps.
Statistics provide quarterly installation counts.
The collection was updated 11 June 2026.
The March 2026 release is official statistics in development.
Scope does not cover every heat-pump technology or capacity.
Installation count is not heat output.
Installation count is not electricity consumption.
Installation count is not direct GHG emissions.
Parcel emissions need operating data and parcel binding.

packages.title: Heat-pump provisional/revision QA
facts: DESNZ states heat-pump deployment statistics are provisional.
The series is subject to future revisions.
The March 2026 release is official statistics in development.
Development status reflects ongoing methodological refinement.
Quarterly counts must retain release edition.
Later revisions can change prior totals.
Provisional deployment must not be labelled final.
Revision does not provide parcel energy use.
Deployment remains an installation count rather than emissions observation.
QA preserves provisional status and technology scope.

packages.title: Heat-pump coverage-change QA
facts: DESNZ announced a coverage change with the December 2025 release.
The series moved toward Total Retrofit UK Heat Pump deployment.
Earlier coverage focused more narrowly on DESNZ-supported deployment.
Individual low-carbon-heating scheme statistics remain separately available.
Coverage change can create a comparability break.
Pre- and post-change counts require definition checks.
Policy-supported installations are not all retrofit installations.
Broader coverage still does not measure operating energy.
Coverage expansion does not provide parcel emissions.
QA retains release-specific coverage definitions.

packages.title: New-dwellings EPC/Part-L statistics-development QA
facts: MHCLG publishes energy-efficiency characteristics of new dwellings in England.
The dataset monitors Part L standards.
January-to-March 2026 data were added 6 May 2026.
Source data come from lodged Energy Performance Certificates.
Statistics include property type and heating systems.
They include heat-pump and solar-PV characteristics.
The series is official statistics in development.
The statistics may be refined after user feedback.
An EPC is not measured operational emissions.
Building EPC evidence is not parcel emissions measurement.

packages.title: New-dwelling technology-feature versus emissions QA
facts: The dataset records selected energy-efficiency technologies.
A heat-pump feature is not annual heat delivered.
A solar-PV feature is not annual electricity generated.
A Part L category is not a measured carbon inventory.
An EPC is an assessment rather than continuous meter data.
Property type does not define land-parcel boundaries.
Technology presence supports modelling only with explicit assumptions.
Operational emissions depend on usage and energy supply.
Modelled emissions must remain labelled modelled.
Parcel emissions require geometry, activity and time-matched evidence.

packages.title: Fuel-poverty LILEE indicator scope QA
facts: DESNZ England fuel-poverty statistics use the LILEE indicator.
The 2026 annual report includes final 2024 estimates.
It analyses characteristics of fuel-poor households.
Fuel poverty combines income and energy-efficiency concepts.
It is a social indicator, not GHG measurement.
Fuel-poor does not necessarily mean high emissions.
Not fuel-poor does not necessarily mean low emissions.
Household indicator data should not be converted directly to parcel emissions.
Indicator year and geography must be retained.
Fuel-poverty data are context, not energy-use evidence.

packages.title: Fuel-poverty final-versus-projection QA
facts: The 2026 report distinguishes final estimates from projections.
It contains final 2024 estimates.
It includes projections for later years.
Projected values must not be labelled observed final statistics.
Fuel-poverty trends cover 2010 to 2025 data.
Detailed tables provide 2025 indicator breakdowns.
Products therefore carry different statuses and reference periods.
Final and projected values must remain separated.
Fuel-poverty projections do not provide parcel energy use.
Parcel emissions are outside LILEE scope.

packages.title: Port-freight Q1-2026 provisional activity QA
facts: DfT published Q1 2026 port-freight statistics on 10 June 2026.
The release covers UK major ports.
Total freight tonnage was 104.7 million tonnes.
Inward tonnage was 72.3 million tonnes.
Outward tonnage was 32.5 million tonnes.
Unitised traffic was 4.7 million units.
The release is provisional.
Port tonnage is activity, not GHG emissions.
Port statistics do not identify terminal-parcel emissions.
Emissions need vessel, fuel, voyage and boundary data.

packages.title: Port-freight tonnage/units versus GHG QA
facts: DfT port statistics report tonnage and unitised traffic.
Tonnage and units are different activity measures.
Neither is direct fuel consumption.
Neither is direct CO2e measurement.
Cargo and vessel efficiency can vary for equal tonnage.
Port-handled freight is not emissions occurring on port land.
Inward and outward traffic should remain separate.
Rolling-year and quarterly values require time-base care.
Activity metrics need explicit emissions assumptions for modelling.
Parcel attribution needs a port-facility geometry gate.

packages.title: Port-freight revision/provider QA
facts: DfT maintains port and waterborne-freight data tables.
Tables were updated 10 June 2026 with Q1 2026 data.
Some historical data were revised after provider engagement.
Revisions affected selected earlier London and Hull data.
Provider revisions are part of series quality control.
Previously downloaded values can become stale.
Quarterly provisional and annual accredited releases differ in status.
Future annual-release announcements are not already published data.
Revision control does not convert activity into emissions.
QA preserves edition, period and provisional/final status.

packages.title: Waste-from-households recycling-rate 2024 QA
facts: Defra published 2024/25 annual waste results on 31 March 2026.
England waste-from-households recycling rate was 43.8% in 2024.
The 2023 rate was 44.0%.
Total household waste was 21.9 million tonnes in 2024.
Recycled household waste was 9.6 million tonnes.
Residual waste treated was 12.3 million tonnes.
These are waste-management statistics, not GHG emissions.
Household totals do not identify individual parcels.
Recycling rate needs lifecycle methodology before CO2e use.
Parcel waste emissions need parcel-specific waste activity.

packages.title: Waste treatment-route boundary QA
facts: Defra reports treatment routes for local-authority collected waste.
In 2024/25, 5.5% was sent to landfill in England.
In 2024/25, 50.3% was sent to incineration.
In 2024/25, 41.2% was sent for recycling.
Incineration includes with and without energy recovery.
Recycling includes recycling, composting, anaerobic digestion or reuse in the cited definition.
Treatment shares are not GHG factors.
Landfill tonnage is not methane emissions.
Incineration tonnage is not stack emissions.
Parcel emissions require treatment-specific emissions evidence.

packages.title: Waste IBA-metal recycling guard QA
facts: Defra includes metal recovered after incineration in household recycling.
IBA metal added about one percentage point to the 2024 recycling rate.
IBA metal recovery is part of the statistical recycling definition.
Incineration and recycling categories can interact through recovered material.
Recycling numerator is not simply material avoiding incineration.
Method definitions must be retained in comparisons.
Recovered metal mass is not direct avoided emissions.
Lifecycle carbon benefit needs separate methodology.
Local-authority recycling does not identify parcel waste generation.
Parcel carbon must not be inferred from headline recycling rate.

packages.title: WasteDataFlow coverage QA
facts: Defra annual waste statistics use WasteDataFlow submissions.
All local authorities in England submit collected/managed waste data.
The publication covers England and regions.
Methodology gives definitions and quality context.
Administrative coverage is not household-by-household parcel coverage.
Local-authority data aggregate many premises.
Waste can be managed outside the authority of origin.
Treatment destination and waste origin are distinct geographies.
Coverage completeness differs from emissions-method completeness.
Parcel emissions need origin and treatment-path evidence.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime first-scheme-year QA
facts: Domestic maritime activity entered UK ETS from 1 July 2026.
The first maritime scheme year is 1 July to 31 December 2026.
From 2027, scheme years run January to December.
First-year maritime data therefore cover half a year.
Half-year 2026 must not be compared blindly to full years.
Operators require an approved emissions monitoring plan.
Scheme scope is operator/activity based, not parcel based.
Maritime emissions can occur away from port parcels.
Port location does not identify voyage emissions.
Parcel accounting needs an explicit maritime boundary rule.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime gas-species/CO2e QA
facts: UK ETS maritime monitoring covers CO2.
It also covers methane.
It also covers nitrous oxide.
Covered gases are expressed in CO2 equivalent.
Maritime gas coverage differs from aviation UK ETS CO2 scope.
CO2e combines gases rather than measuring one gas.
Eligible fuel can affect an emissions-reduction claim.
Operator emissions are not port-parcel emissions.
Gas-species boundaries must be retained.
Parcel attribution needs separate spatial/operational accounting.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime surrender-timing QA
facts: Maritime emissions reports are due by 31 March following the scheme year.
Allowances correspond to the emissions figure for surrender after deductions.
For 2026 and 2027 scheme years, the cited surrender deadline is 30 April 2028.
From 2028 onward, surrender is due 30 April of the following year.
Reporting and surrender dates are distinct.
Monitoring precedes later allowance surrender.
Allowance transactions are compliance records, not direct measurement.
Surrender quantity is not parcel energy use.
Registry and emissions data require period alignment.
Parcel attribution remains a separate gate.

packages.title: UK ETS HSE target-versus-allowance QA
facts: Hospital and Small Emitters can use a simplified UK ETS route.
HSEs do not surrender allowances for emissions.
HSEs are not entitled to free allocation.
They receive annual emissions targets.
Targets are included in HSE permits.
Reportable emissions are compared with annual targets.
A target is not actual emissions.
A permit boundary is not automatically one cadastral parcel.
Compliance status does not identify parcel energy use.
Parcel emissions need installation-to-parcel matching.

packages.title: UK ETS HSE threshold/target-data QA
facts: A non-hospital small emitter generally must emit below 25,000 tCO2e per relevant scheme year.
Where applicable, rated thermal input must be below 35 MW.
Hospital-service installations have separate eligibility conditions.
Hospital-service qualification can use an 85% heat-supply test.
HSE targets can use bankable amounts within an allocation period.
Bankable amounts do not carry between allocation periods.
DESNZ published HSE target and actual-emissions data through 2025 in June 2026.
Target and actual-emission rows must stay distinct.
Installation data are not automatically parcel data.
Eligibility thresholds are not substitutes for measured emissions.

packages.title: UK ETS ultra-small-emitter threshold/monitoring QA
facts: Ultra-Small Emitter status applies to qualifying low-emission installations.
The cited threshold is below 2,500 tCO2e.
USE installations must continue monitoring emissions.
They must notify the regulator if the threshold is exceeded.
USE status depends on the qualifying list for the allocation period.
Aircraft operators cannot use this USE route.
The threshold is an eligibility rule, not a parcel value.
An installation boundary need not equal one cadastral parcel.
Monitoring evidence must retain scheme year and installation boundary.
Parcel emissions need explicit installation-to-parcel geometry matching.
